info.title: Meridian API
info.description: Everything the web panel does, as JSON over HTTP. Authenticate with an API token (Authorization: Bearer mrd_...) or the supervisor's browser session. Users who sign in to their own page reach only the User page operations. Errors are {"error": "..."} with a 4xx/5xx status.

tags.description: Sign-in, password, two-factor and browser sessions. Cookie sessions need the header X-Meridian: 1 on every non-GET request (CSRF protection).
tags.name: Session

tags.description: Tokens for scripts and AI assistants: Authorization: Bearer <token>. Read tokens may only GET.
tags.name: API tokens

tags.description: Who is connected, from where, through which subscription, and where the traffic goes.
tags.name: Monitoring

tags.description: Servers run the agent; everything on them is applied live unless an action says otherwise.
tags.name: Servers

tags.description: VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, SOCKS5, HTTP, Hysteria2 and WireGuard, over raw TCP, WebSocket, gRPC, HTTPUpgrade or XHTTP with TLS, REALITY or a CDN - only combinations that work. Includes proxy pass.

tags.name: Users

post.description: One sign-in for everyone: the supervisor gets the panel session (kind admin), a user gets their own page (kind user, a separate cookie). Needs the X-Meridian: 1 header. With two-factor sign-in, the first answer is {totp_required: true}; send the same request again with code.

get.summary: Panel name, and for signed-in callers version and protocol catalogue
Browsers signed in to your account

post.description: The token is returned once. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

get.description: Client IPs that connected, aggregated per IP, most recent first (at most 1000). q matches an IP prefix, organisation, city or country code.
Where traffic went, by bytes then connections (at most 500). Bytes are exact for WireGuard; Xray and Hysteria2 report connections.

parameters.description: Only events with a smaller id (paging)
parameters.name: before

post.description: Returns the install command to run on the server. protocols lists what to set up once the agent connects.

delete.description: The agent removes everything Meridian set up and uninstalls itself. Everyone on the server is disconnected.

post.description: The agent cannot reach the panel until it is reinstalled with the new command. Traffic is not affected.

Queues an explicit maintenance action. restart_pending restarts exactly what waits for a restart (the server's pending_restart) and disconnects those users for a moment; restart_xray and upgrade_xray disconnect Xray users for a moment; upgrade_hysteria and upgrade_realm switch the server to the version in Settings and restart those cores (their users reconnect); upgrade_agent disconnects nobody.

get.description: Protocols with their transports and security layers, the apps the panel writes subscriptions for, and the choices for fingerprints, XHTTP modes and certificates.

post.summary: Check a protocol before adding it
post.description: Says whether the combination can be saved (and if not, why and what to do instead), how apps will name it, its usual ports, which apps can use it and what the admin needs to do. Nothing is stored.

post.summary: Add a protocol to a server
post.description: Applied live without restarting anything. Only combinations that work can be saved (POST /api/protocols/check shows why one cannot). Port 0 picks a free common port. REALITY camouflage is checked from the server.

patch.description: Only the given fields change; the result must still be a working combination. Changing the transport, security or certificate means devices must refresh their subscription.

post.description: New REALITY keys, self-signed certificate, Shadowsocks server key or WireGuard key. Every device using the protocol must refresh its subscription.

post.summary: Check a REALITY camouflage site from the server
Look for proxy software already on the server
post.description: The agent reads (and changes nothing) the configs of Xray, V2Ray, 3x-ui and x-ui, sing-box and Hysteria2. Poll the action, then GET the scan.

get.description: Programs, their protocols, ports and user names, and whether each can be imported. Keys and passwords are never shown.

post.summary: Import protocols found by the scan
post.description: Each detected user becomes a Meridian user (or is matched by name) and keeps their credentials, keys and certificate. With take_over the old service is stopped and the same ports are served, so devices keep working; without it nothing is stopped and busy ports are moved.

get.summary: List shared certificates, the protocols using each and where each server stands with it
A shared certificate, with per-server status

patch.summary: Rename or replace a shared certificate - one call updates every server that uses it (for renewal hooks)

delete.summary: Remove a shared certificate that no protocol uses

get.summary: The Xray configuration a server gets, with your code merged in (users left out)

post.description: Each user gets a subscription link and, unless sign_in is false, a username and password for their own page. A generated password is returned once. count > 1 creates name-01, name-02, ... Quota, expiry and IP limit only raise alerts; nothing is paused automatically.

patch.description: Only the given fields change. A new username or password signs the user out everywhere; an empty username removes the sign-in.

post.summary: Pause, resume, new link, new credentials, reset usage, sign out or new password
post.description: pause disconnects every device now; resume lets them back; rotate-link replaces the link (old one stops working); reset-keys gives new credentials (devices must refresh); reset-usage zeroes this cycle; sign-out ends the user's sessions on their own page; new-password generates a sign-in password (and a username if there is none) and returns it once.

get.summary: IPs that used this user's link
The signed-in user's link, limits, devices and usage per server

post.description: Signs the user out everywhere else.

get.summary: Every server for the live dashboard
get.description: The status page's dashboard: servers (name, place, public IP addresses, up or down, availability over 24 hours and 30 days, throughput, load, memory, disk, connections, monthly bandwidth and traffic, expiry date, system), totals, traffic per day and outages. Visitors get it while the status page shows the servers to everyone; the supervisor always. IP addresses are in it only while the status page shows them (status_ips, off by default) - then for everyone, otherwise for nobody. Nothing about users, protocols, ports, keys or prices.

get.summary: Throughput per server since a time
Cities for setting a server's location by hand
Country rules for the servers and for this site
get.description: Both rules, what each server follows, devices connected now by country, packets the servers' rule refused today and requests this site refused.

put.description: block refuses the listed countries; allow admits only them. It covers every protocol and forward (SSH is never touched), applies within seconds and also cuts connections that are already open. Servers with their own rule (PATCH /api/servers/{id} country_mode) keep it. Private networks and the panel's own servers always get in.

put.summary: Set who may open this site
put.description: The same kind of rule for the panel, the users' pages, the status page and subscription links. Agents are never refused. A rule that would lock out the address you send it from is refused.

post.description: Applies to every protocol and forward on every server and drops open connections. SSH and other services are not affected.

put.description: Send only the fields to change; the others keep their values. Core version changes never restart servers - upgrade each server explicitly.

The raw image as the body: SVG, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 128 KB and 2048 x 2048 pixels. It replaces the built-in umbrella everywhere - top bar, sign-in, loading screens, status page, subscription pages and the browser tab. SVGs may only draw (no scripts, links or outside resources): the answer says what to remove otherwise.

delete.summary: Use the built-in umbrella logo again

get.summary: Notifications: where they go and what is sent
get.description: The bot token and the webhook come back masked - they are never shown again in full.

put.description: New events of the chosen groups are sent as they happen, in order; turning notifications on never sends the past. Omitted fields keep their value; an empty token or webhook removes it. Webhooks must be HTTPS. Nothing is ever paused by them - they only tell.

post.summary: Send a test message through every channel that is set up
Chats that wrote to the bot lately
post.description: Send the bot a message (or add it to a group) first; then pick the chat from this list instead of looking up its id. The body may carry a token that is not saved yet.

get.summary: Updates: this panel's version, the newest release, and servers with an older agent

post.summary: Look for a new release now

post.description: The panel downloads the release, checks its signature (Meridian's release key) and checksum, backs up the database and hands it to the updater service, which checks it again and installs it. Proxies keep running; the panel restarts once. With agents (the default), every server's agent is upgraded afterwards - nobody is disconnected. Needs a panel installed with install-panel.sh.

post.summary: Upgrade every server's agent to this panel's version
post.description: Only servers whose agent differs from the panel's are upgraded; offline ones as soon as they connect. Agents restart themselves; the proxies keep running and nobody is disconnected.

get.summary: The uploaded logo (404 while the built-in one is used)
The browser tab icon: the uploaded logo, or the built-in one
A subscription, in the format the app needs
get.description: The app is detected from its User-Agent; ?client= forces a format. Browsers get a page with QR codes and import buttons. Headers carry Subscription-Userinfo (usage, quota, expiry).

post.description: Streamable HTTP transport (JSON-RPC 2.0, JSON responses, stateless). Needs an API token; read-only tokens only see read tools. Tools that disconnect people require confirm=true.

loc_manual.description: The location was set by hand (not from the IP database)

addrs.description: The addresses on the server's own interfaces, as the agent reports them: what a protocol can be bound to

xray_code.description: Your own Xray configuration (JSON, comments allowed), merged on top of what the panel generates: outbounds (added, or replacing one with the same tag), routing.rules (before the panel's), inbounds by tag (merged into that protocol, or added as your own) and other sections (dns, ...). Only the syntax is checked; Xray decides the rest

desired_rev.description: The configuration the panel wants on the server: it is in place when applied_rev equals it

limits.description: What does not work on this server, and how to change that

loc_from.description: The address whose DB-IP entry gives the location: the address when it was set by hand to an IP, otherwise the IP the agent reports (empty when the location was set by hand)

acme_port.description: The TCP port Let's Encrypt's check arrives on - 80, or where the provider forwards port 80 - when a protocol gets its certificate from Let's Encrypt (its firewall must let it in); 0 when none does

settings.description: The protocol's settings without private keys

pass_only.description: Serves only proxy passes from other servers: users cannot connect to it directly and it is left out of their links

bind_ip.description: The server address this protocol has to itself: it listens there, its traffic leaves from there and links use it (a public one). Empty = all of the server's addresses

code.description: The protocol's own settings, merged on top of what the panel generates: JSON for Xray protocols (inbound fields, outbounds, rules for its traffic), YAML for Hysteria2. Only the syntax is checked

label.description: How apps name it, e.g. REALITY or VLESS WS TLS

apps.description: Which apps can use it as configured

notes.description: What the admin needs to know or do

pass_name.description: The proxy pass exit, as 'server · protocol'

pass_broken.description: Why the proxy pass cannot be used right now (the exit is turned off or removed); its traffic is blocked meanwhile

pass_entries.description: Protocols on other servers that pass through this one, as 'server · protocol'

public_port.description: The port devices connect to, when the server's provider forwards it under another number than port
The port devices connect to, when the server's provider forwards the listen port under another number

address.description: Domain or IP clients connect to; empty = the IP the agent reports

bw_limit.description: Monthly bandwidth in bytes, for alerts only; 0 = unlimited

bw_mode.description: What counts: both | up | down | max

bw_reset_day.description: Day of the month the cycle restarts (1-31)

bw_offset.description: Bytes to add to this cycle (to match the provider's meter)

country_mode.description: Country rule: '' = follow the global rule, off = none, block or allow = its own (with countries)

public_name.description: Name on the status page; empty = the server's name

status_hidden.description: Leave the server off the status page

location.description: Set the location by hand (the globe and the status page); send {} with auto_location to go back

auto_location.description: Go back to the location from the IP database

countries.description: With country_mode block or allow: two-letter country codes

protocols.description: On create, optional: protocols to set up with their default settings (vless, vmess, trojan, shadowsocks, hysteria2, wireguard, socks, http)

xray_code.description: Your own Xray configuration (JSON, comments allowed), merged on top of what the panel generates. Only the syntax is checked; empty removes it

ip_version.description: '' = IPv4 and IPv6 (the default), ipv4 = IPv4 only, ipv6 = IPv6 only: how protocols reach sites, which address links use, and whether WireGuard may route IPv6. Xray takes it live; Hysteria2 protocols restart once

public_ports.description: Only for servers whose provider decides their ports (NAT servers, LXC and Incus containers): the ports it forwards, e.g. '20000-20019'; PUBLIC:LOCAL where the number on the server differs ('40001-40010:10001-10010'); /tcp or /udp where only one is forwarded. Protocols and forwards then use only these ports and links carry the public numbers. Empty = every port

install.description: One-line agent install command; contains the agent's secret. Omitted for read-only tokens

kind.description: restart_pending | restart_xray | upgrade_xray | upgrade_hysteria | upgrade_realm | upgrade_agent

cdn_origin_ports.description: Ports Cloudflare forwards over plain HTTP

kind.description: vless | vmess | trojan | shadowsocks | hysteria2 | wireguard | socks | http

node_id.description: Editing: the protocol being changed. The draft is checked as a change to it - omitted fields and keys keep their stored values, as saving does

port.description: Editing: the port it would have (omitted: unchanged)

bind_ip.description: Editing: its own address it would have (omitted: unchanged)

code.description: Editing: its own settings as code (omitted: unchanged)

flow.description: VLESS over raw with TLS or REALITY: xtls-rprx-vision, or empty

sni.description: TLS: certificate name. REALITY: the camouflage site. Hysteria2: certificate name

fingerprint.description: Browser fingerprint clients present: chrome, firefox, safari, ...

target.description: REALITY: where unauthenticated visitors go, host:port

cert_mode.description: TLS and Hysteria2: self | acme | custom | shared

cert_id.description: With cert_mode shared: the shared certificate (GET /api/certs)

dns_logging.description: WireGuard: clients use the server's logging resolver

error.description: Why the combination cannot be saved

label.description: How the protocol is named in apps

notes.description: What the admin needs to know or do

settings.description: The settings as they would be saved (keys left out)

kind.description: On create: vless | vmess | trojan | shadowsocks | hysteria2 | wireguard | socks | http

port.description: 0 or omitted on create = pick a free common port

host.description: Address override for this protocol only; empty = the server's address

pass_only.description: Serve only proxy passes from other servers: users cannot connect directly and it is left out of their links (not for WireGuard)

code.description: The protocol's own settings, merged on top of what the panel generates. Xray protocols: JSON (comments allowed) - fields merged into the inbound (sniffing, streamSettings.sockopt, fallbacks, ...), outbounds added (own tags), rules for this protocol's traffic only; tag, port and users stay the panel's. Hysteria2: YAML; auth and trafficStats stay the panel's (saving restarts it). Only the syntax is checked; empty removes it

bind_ip.description: One of the server's addresses (see addrs on the server) for this protocol alone: it listens there, its traffic leaves from there, and links use it when it is public. Protocols on different addresses may share a port. Empty = all addresses

settings.description: Transport, security and the protocol's own options; omitted fields keep their value (or the default on create). POST /api/protocols/check shows what a draft becomes

auto.description: Switch a new protocol (less than a day old) to the fastest working site

telegram_chat.description: The chat to write to: a numeric id (a group's is negative) or @channelname

webhook_url.description: An HTTPS address that receives a JSON POST ({text, content, events}) per batch; omit to keep the current one, empty to remove it

groups.description: What to send: servers, users, certificates, security

telegram.description: ok, or why it failed; empty when Telegram is not set up

webhook.description: ok, or why it failed; empty when no webhook is set up

latest.description: The newest release (empty until the first check)

newer.description: Whether the newest release is newer than this panel

auto_update.description: Whether new releases install by themselves (Settings › auto_update)

ready.description: Whether this panel can install updates itself

not_ready.description: Why it cannot, and what to do

state.description: idle | downloading (the panel fetches and checks the release) | installing (the updater service has it; the panel restarts)

error.description: Why the last update request failed

outdated_agents.description: Servers whose agent is not this panel's version

agents.description: Also upgrade every server's agent once the new panel runs (default true; nobody is disconnected)

servers.description: The servers whose agent upgrades now

error.description: What went wrong, in plain English
